newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil eases, Russians offered.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil eases, Russians offered.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges and cargoes were easier again on Monday amid lacklustre demand and good supply of Russian material, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $103 and $104 fob ARA amid poor demand for bunkers.
High sulphur cargoes were relatively thin after business late last week at around $105/$106 cif NWE, but dealers said that utility bids had fallen away to below barge levels.
One U.K. utility was heard looking for a cargo loading in the first half of February and was only willing to pay $101 cif NWE.
Dealers said E-4 cargoes were well supplied, with two high water pieces loading this month out of Klaipeda, as well as one low water out of St Petersburg and another out of Ventspils.
This latter cargo was bought on Friday by an ARA refiner at around $3 or $4 over the three means of quotes. An M-100 and an M-40 were also heard loading in the Baltics this month.
Low sulphur fuel oil was softer amid slack demand.
A Scandinavian player with a low sulphur straight-run cargo was heard receiving quotes-related bids from a couple of NWE refiners. The seller was thought seeking around $135 fob NWE.
